blocks.x: Guests judge a hotel in minutes: the lobby, the hallway, the room, the bathroom. Online reviews then tell everyone else. For independent and branded hotels alike, a well-planned hotel renovation in Winnipeg, MB aims to lift ratings, rates and repeat stays. A hotel renovation without closing depends on phasing, so the rest of the property keeps welcoming guests.
Upgrades guests notice
**Guest bathrooms.** Guests look closely here. New vanities, good lighting, fresh grout and modern fixtures change how a room feels.
**Beds, lighting and outlets.** Reading lights, bedside charging and enough well-placed outlets are small details guests notice.
**Flooring.** [Replacing worn carpet](/services/flooring) with durable hard surfaces or new carpet tile updates rooms and corridors and simplifies cleaning.

**Windows and comfort.** Drafty windows and noisy heating units hurt sleep, especially in a Winnipeg winter. [Window replacement](/services/windows-and-doors) and quieter, better-controlled room heating can pay off in reviews and energy bills.
**Lobby and arrival.** Lighting, seating, a refreshed front desk and a clean, bright entrance shape the first impression.
**Smart, simple technology.** Mobile key entry, strong Wi-Fi, smart thermostats that reset when rooms are empty, and leak sensors in bathrooms can improve guest experience and lower operating costs.
Back-of-house upgrades to consider
Commercial laundry and housekeeping areas laid out to speed room turns
Efficient lighting and controls in corridors and parkades
Durable finishes in high-traffic areas
Accessibility upgrades for guest rooms, washrooms and public areas
How to keep your hotel open during a renovation
**Renovate in room blocks.** Take one floor or wing out of inventory at a time.
**Time it with demand.** Plan the heaviest work for slower periods and avoid major Winnipeg event dates.

**Control noise and dust.** Set quiet hours, seal work areas and use separate routes for crews. The [City's noise hours](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/property-records/construction-your-neighbourhood) apply within 150 metres of a home: 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday to Friday, and 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekends and holidays. Keep noisy tasks to daytime hours.

**Keep accessible rooms and routes working.** If a ramp, automatic door or elevator has to go out of service, Manitoba's [Accessible Customer Service Standard](https://accessibilitymb.ca/resources/cs-standard/general/cs-handbook.pdf) requires telling the public why, when it's due back and how else they can get service.
**Keep guests informed.** Clear notices at booking and check-in help avoid surprises and bad reviews.
**Build a model room first.** It locks in finishes and reveals installation issues before you repeat them across dozens of rooms.
Permits and code

Hotel renovations in Winnipeg often require City of Winnipeg building, plumbing and electrical permits. Changes to fire separations, sprinklers, alarms and accessibility must meet current code, and [significant fire separation or fire safety work can call for drawings sealed by an architect or engineer](https://www.winnipeg.ca/media/6330). Plan permit time into your schedule.
In an older building, have suspect materials [tested for asbestos](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba) before work disturbs them.

Altered floors can need an occupancy permit too. The City requires one for [substantial alterations to most buildings](https://legacy.winnipeg.ca/PPD/permits/Commercial/OccupancyPermits.stm), and its list of who needs one includes an occupant who has to vacate a floor or wing for alterations. Ask the City early whether your phases trigger one. Our [occupancy permit guide](/blog/occupancy-permit-change-of-use-winnipeg) explains how it works.

Accessible rooms belong in the plan from the start. Manitoba adopted the 2020 National Building Code on January 1, 2024, with accessibility updates aligned with the CSA B651 standard, and the [Manitoba Building Code](https://web2.gov.mb.ca/laws/regs/current/078-2023.php?lang=en) applies to the part of an existing building that is altered. This is general information, not legal advice: the City decides what applies to your project.
The bottom line
The best hotel renovations focus on what guests see, touch and sleep in, and are phased to protect revenue.
